mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision date reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing near-term S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during pre-tightening periods (t-test p > 0.05) when trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which boosts consumer confidence and equity valuations, driving positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by > 10,000 jobs while UNRATE falls by > 0.2 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: Significant negative 20-day returns occur despite the labor indicators meeting or exceeding the trigger thresholds.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 1,200K for three consecutive months indicates expanding building activity, which is a leading indicator of consumer and business confidence, predicting positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 200-day rolling average when HOUST remains elevated.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in the month before the decision date suggests weakening demand or supply-side headwinds that compress earnings expectations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% in a single month
failure_condition: No significant negative returns when INDPRO declines by the specified amount.

mechanism_narrative: When the annual inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a near-term rate hike, which reduces the present value of equities and drives negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not statistically lower than during periods of similar inflation expectations (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% followed by a sustained increase in job openings (PAYEMS) above 7 million indicates a tight labor market, which can drive equity valuations up and produce positive 20-day S&P 500 returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% and PAYEMS > 7M for the next month
failure_condition: 20-day returns show no significant improvement relative to the pre-trigger period.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales (implied via a proxy such as GDPC1) of over 2% suggests weakening consumer demand, which lowers earnings growth forecasts and results in negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by > 2% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day returns are not significantly lower than during normal demand cycles (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling industrial production (INDPRO) for two consecutive months, the market anticipates a supply shock that reduces corporate profit expectations, producing negative 20-day S&P 500 returns regardless of other macro signals.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day returns are not persistently negative across multiple such regimes.
